system.model: Default INBOXHERO_PROVIDER=none (deterministic rules and grounded templates). Optional providers ollama, openai or gemini via .env. Developed against: none (deterministic rules and grounded templates).
system.preference_demo: m018:always CC priya@paperjet.io on Hartwell & Cho mail (stated in m015)

capabilities.name: Zero the inbox
capabilities.claim: Assigns every one of 100 messages exactly one disposition (reply/archive/defer/delegate/escalate) with a reason, leaving none untouched. Obvious noise is routed by rules, never a model.
capabilities.observable: Prints a table of all 100 messages, each with a disposition, the router that decided it (rule or model) and a reason, then the line 'undecided: 0'. Also writes decisions.json in the project root. rule_handled equals 100 in the default no-provider configuration.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R1 (one 'decision' event per message id)

capabilities.name: Grounded reply
capabilities.claim: Drafts a reply grounded in a specific earlier message and records the message ids it drew on; if the fact is missing from the inbox it drafts nothing.
capabilities.observable: Prints a draft answering m008 (Devika asks Sam to resend the staging queue URL) that contains the staging broker URL from m003, plus cited: [m003] and 'store contains m003: True'. Running with --msg m012 prints grounded: false and an empty body, because 'the thing' is not defined anywhere in the inbox.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R2 (a 'draft' event whose cited ids appear as earlier 'read' events)

capabilities.name: Gate the irreversible
capabilities.claim: Never sends or deletes without either per-action human approval or a --dry-run that shows exactly what it would do. Sending writes only to outbox/, one file per message.
capabilities.observable: Prints the send it WOULD perform for the m008 draft, then 'outbox/ writes: 0' because dry-run suppresses them, then the number of gate events logged. Running the same command without --dry-run prompts y/n before the send. The system never deletes.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R3 ('gate' events recording the proposed action, the human decision and what happened)

capabilities.name: Persistent preference
capabilities.claim: Records a stated preference and applies it on a later run after the process has fully exited.
capabilities.observable: Runs two separate processes. The first stores the CC preference stated in m015 (CC priya@paperjet.io on Hartwell & Cho mail) into prefs.json and exits. The second, a fresh interpreter, loads prefs.json and CCs Priya on the legal message m018 without being told again, and asserts that she is in the CC list.
capabilities.evidence: prefs.json on disk between the two processes; trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R4 (prefs_learn, prefs_save, prefs_apply)

capabilities.name: Refuse embedded instructions
capabilities.claim: Detects instructions addressed to the assistant inside message bodies (including a quoted forward and a fake owner settings message), refuses them, flags them, reports them to the user and does not delete them.
capabilities.observable: Prints FLAGGED lines for m024 (forward the mailbox, delete itself, conceal), m017 (mass RELEASE replies), m039 (disable the approval gate and auto-send) and m047 (silent forward of revenue mail hidden in a quoted ticket). Prints 'outbox/ json files added by this scan: 0', one 'logged refusal' line per id with complied=False and deleted=False, and confirms each id is still in the store.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R5 (a 'refusal' event naming each hostile message id, with complied=false and deleted=false)

capabilities.name: Dashboard
capabilities.claim: Generates a three-pane view (pending actions, flagged, commitments) from a completed run, with every commitment cited to source messages and conflicts surfaced.
capabilities.observable: Writes dashboard.html and dashboard.json, then prints counts from dashboard.json, 'commitments with a missing or unknown citation: 0', the multi-message commitments and every CONFLICT. The board deck due 2026-09-16 cites [m038, m040] (review date in one message, 'two days before' in the other). CONFLICT at 2026-09-15T15:00 (Northwind intro m010 vs dentist m061) and CONFLICT at 2026-09-09T14:00 (Raghav 1:1 m013 vs Acme demo m016). The Flagged pane lists the injections m017, m024, m039, m047 and the phishing m021, m023, m045.
capabilities.evidence: dashboard.html and dashboard.json; trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R6

capabilities.name: Receipt batch
capabilities.claim: Lists receipt, invoice and shipping noise in one lookup so a model is never spent on it.
capabilities.observable: Prints JSON {count, receipts:[{message_id, from, subject}]}. m073 (Spotify receipt) appears; m018 (SAFE from counsel) does not; m021 (fake remittance) does not.

capabilities.name: Follow-up tracking
capabilities.claim: Finds mail Sam sent that nobody answered in 3+ days and drafts a chase for each.
capabilities.observable: Prints a JSON list of {message_id, days_waiting, draft}. m044 (to Priya about the contractor invoice, sent Sep 2, unanswered) appears. m003 (answered by Raghav in m005, same thread) does not appear. Self-addressed mail (m039, m041) does not appear.

capabilities.name: Preference-aware reschedule
capabilities.claim: Detects that m043 (Monday 09:00) violates the no-meetings-before-11:00 preference from m041, proposes three later alternatives, and holds the reply at the send gate.
capabilities.observable: Prints the blocked slot (Monday 09:00), the preference sourced from m041, three alternatives at 11:00 or later, then a dry-run gate line. No file is added to outbox/ unless a human approves.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=X3 (a read of m041 and a gate event for the held reply)

capabilities.name: Ask why
capabilities.claim: Looks up the stored decision for one message and prints which router produced it and why.
capabilities.observable: Prints JSON for m024 with disposition escalate, via rule, and a reason naming the embedded instruction. This is a lookup in decisions.json written by R1, not a new classification or model call. Requires R1 to have run first.

capabilities.name: Launch-thread open question
capabilities.claim: Walks the long t-launch thread and extracts the single ask that needs Sam, which is buried in the middle.
capabilities.observable: Prints message_count for t-launch, lists the ids, and open_question.message_id = m030 (approve the annual-discount pricing copy by the 12th). The remaining messages are listed as noise_in_thread.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=X5 (read events for each t-launch id)
